item.title: Portrait Cut for Two Speakers

turns.text: Turn this into a 9:16 vertical clip. Show the man when he asks his question, then the woman when she answers, with each centred while talking. Keep all 10 seconds and the original audio. No captions.

item.tests: Tests speaker-aware portrait reframing of a two-person conversation without losing either speaking turn.

answer_sheet.Source and speakers: Use talk-two.mp4. The man asks the question and the woman answers.
answer_sheet.Layout and transitions: Centre the current speaker in a full-frame portrait crop; a clean cut at the speaker change is fine.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, all 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Audio and text: Preserve the original conversation and sound, with no captions or added text.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 portrait edit of the attached office conversation.
The man is centred and his face is fully visible during his question.
The woman is centred and her face is fully visible during her answer.
Both speaking turns remain in their original order, with the full 10 seconds and original audio in sync.
The image is not stretched and contains no added captions.

turns.text: Turn this clip into a 9:16 vertical clip. Show the man when he asks his question, then the woman when she answers, with each centred while talking. Keep all 10 seconds and the original audio. No captions. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**Nothing has run, and no credits have been spent.**

This is a **crop-and-reframe edit**, not an AI-generation task: keep the full 10 seconds, switch the crop from the man to the woman at the speaker change, centre each speaker, preserve the original audio, and add no captions.

The connected Magic Hour tools don’t expose a standard crop/reframe operation. Its generative video editor would spend credits and isn’t a reliable way to preserve the footage and audio exactly. I can’t verify an exact credit quote for that edit, so I won’t submit it.

**The cheapest option is a free local video editor: 0 Magic Hour credits.** In an editor such as Shotcut or DaVinci Resolve:
1. Set the canvas to **9:16**.
2. Split at the speaker change; crop and centre the man first, then the woman.
3. Leave the original audio untouched and export all **10 seconds**, without captions.

For a smaller file, export at **480 × 854**. You don’t need to shorten it or lose any dialogue. A shorter version would conflict with your requirement to keep all 10 seconds; a lower-resolution export is the better saving here.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option is **0 Magic Hour credits**, but I can’t run a local video editor from this chat. I should have made that limitation clearer. **Nothing has run or spent credits.**

To do it free in **Shotcut**:
1. Open the clip and set **Settings → Video Mode → Custom** to **480 × 854**.
2. Split the video where the woman starts answering.
3. Apply **Size, Position & Rotate** to each section: fill the vertical frame and centre the man in the first section, then the woman in the second.
4. Keep both sections’ original audio, add no text, and export the full **10 seconds** as MP4.

I won’t substitute a credit-consuming AI edit for the free option you approved.
